delta: SEPT 4: 10Y yield rose nearly 3bps to 4.79% after the August jobs blowout, reversing Waller's Sept 3 dovish-driven dip.
deltaNote: JULY 23-SEPT 4 ARC: The Red Sea/Hormuz oil shock (Brent >$100, July 23) pushed yields to a multi-month high as September Fed-hike odds jumped to ~82%. The Aug 7 jobs report and Aug 12-13 CPI/PPI prints both cooled, pulling the 10Y down to 4.65%. The Aug 14 Hormuz tanker attacks and Aug 17 MOU expiration pushed the 30-year to 5.31-5.32% (highest since June 2007). Warsh's Aug 28 hawkish Jackson Hole keynote and an Aug 31 Hormuz strike pushed yields higher again, and the rout went fully global Sept 2 (10Y 4.814%, highest since Nov 2023; Japan 10Y above 3% for the first time since 1996; German Bund and UK gilts at multi-year highs). Fed Governor Waller's Sept 3 remarks signaling openness to a September hold pulled yields down briefly, but the Sept 4 jobs blowout (+162,000, June/July revised up 55,000 combined) reversed that within a day, sending the 10Y back to 4.79% as hike odds jumped to ~58%. A renewed US-Iran Gulf conflict (Sept 1-6, spreading to Kuwait, the UAE, and mutual Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes) keeps an oil-driven inflation premium under the long end heading into the Sept 16-17 FOMC.
